headline: States sue Musk companies over flood of sexualized images made with AI chatbot Grok
summary: Two Democratic attorneys general are suing several of Elon Musk's companies in connection with the controversy over his AI chatbot's ability to create sexualized images. Virginia and Oregon argue in lawsuits filed Monday that Musk's companies disregarded safety while building and rolling out the chatbot Grok in ways that allowed proliferation of harmful sexualized imagery, including child abuse material. The lawsuits bring claims under the state's consumer protection statutes. SpaceXSI says it has filed three lawsuits against users it accuses of abusing the platform to create nonconsensual sexually explicit images and child sexual abuse material.

subheadings: SpaceXSI says it worked to curb creation of sexualized content
Lawsuits say company misled the world about its efforts
States sued under consumer protection laws
paragraphs: RICHMOND, Va. (AP) — Elon Musk’s businesses harmed consumers by avoiding safeguards when they designed and launched an artificial intelligence chatbot capable of creating sexualized images, two Democratic attorneys general argued in lawsuits filed Monday.

The choices that went into building Grok led to a proliferation of child sexual abuse material and other nonconsensual intimate imagery on the companies’ platforms, the lawsuits said. The companies prioritized their business model over the safety of millions of people, Virginia Attorney General Jay Jones said in his state’s lawsuit.

“To push its lagging product, Grok, to tens of millions of new users, it stripped out industry-standard safeguards and marketed a ‘spicy mode’ built to produce nudity,” Jones said in the lawsuit. “For these Defendants, weak safeguards were not a failure but a feature.”
Oregon also filed a lawsuit Monday. The attorneys general brought their separate but similar cases under their states’ consumer protection statutes.
The lawsuits named as defendants several Musk companies and subsidiaries, including SpaceX, the social platform X, and SpaceX Super Intelligence, or SpaceXSI, the AI subsidiary of SpaceX.

In a statement, SpaceXSI said sexual content involving minors, “whether real or AI-generated, is abhorrent. It has no place on X or in Grok, and neither do explicit images of real people made without their consent.”

RICHMOND, Va. (AP) — Elon Musk’s businesses harmed consumers by avoiding safeguards when they designed and launched [an artificial intelligence chatbot](https://apnews.com/article/grok-ai-elon-musk-xai-f3f8195a17698aefc517e43da973f2ea) capable of creating sexualized images, two Democratic attorneys general argued in lawsuits filed Monday.

The choices that went into building Grok led to a proliferation of child sexual abuse material and other nonconsensual intimate imagery on the companies’ platforms, the lawsuits said. The companies prioritized their business model over the safety of millions of people, Virginia Attorney General Jay Jones said in his state’s lawsuit.

“To push its lagging product, Grok, to tens of millions of new users, it stripped out industry-standard safeguards and marketed a ‘spicy mode’ built to produce nudity,” Jones said in the lawsuit. “For these Defendants, weak safeguards were not a failure but a feature.”

Oregon also filed a lawsuit Monday. The attorneys general brought their separate but similar cases under their states’ consumer protection statutes.

The lawsuits named as defendants several Musk companies and subsidiaries, including SpaceX, the social platform X, and SpaceX Super Intelligence, or SpaceXSI, the AI [subsidiary of SpaceX](https://apnews.com/article/spacex-xai-musk-space-2079f03fa888652b7fe836afe8b670a1).

## SpaceXSI says it worked to curb creation of sexualized content

In a statement, SpaceXSI said sexual content involving minors, “whether real or AI-generated, is abhorrent. It has no place on X or in Grok, and neither do explicit images of real people made without their consent.”
